facts.statement: The only known species in the genus is Archaeopsittacus verreauxi.
The genus Archaeopsittacus was named by Lambrecht in 1933.
Fossils of Archaeopsittacus were found at Verreaux near Saint-Gérand-le-Puy, France.
facts.quote: It is known from deposits of either Late Oligocene or Early Miocene age (c. 23 mya) at Verreaux near Saint-Gérand-le-Puy, France.

facts.statement: Archaeopsittacus lived during the Late Oligocene or Early Miocene, approximately 23 million years ago.
facts.quote: It is known from deposits of either Late Oligocene or Early Miocene age (c. 23 mya)

facts.statement: Archaeopsittacus is thought to be closely related to Old World parrots and may belong to the superfamily Psittacoidea.
facts.quote: The genus was apparently close to the Old World lineages of parrots and might conceivably be assigned to the modern superfamily Psittacoidea.

facts.statement: Scientists cannot definitively classify Archaeopsittacus beyond the superfamily Psittacoidea because there are not enough unique physical traits in the fossils.
facts.quote: Its lack of apomorphies prevents any better placement until more material is found.
